He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. ==High school career== [[File:20170329 MCDAAG Trevon Duval dribbling (1).jpg|thumb|left|Duval at the [[2017 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2017 McDonald's All-American Game]]]] Duval attended [[St. Benedict's Preparatory School]] in [[Newark, New Jersey]] during his Freshman and Sophomore years. As a sophomore in 2014–15, Duval led the Gray Bees to a 31–6 record and NCSAA state championship in which he scored 25 [[Point guard|points]] and had 8 [[assist (basketball)|assists]]. Prior to his sophomore year, Duval along with [[Isaiah Briscoe]] for the AAU team, New Jersey Playaz won the 2014 [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]] Elite Youth Basketball League (EYBL) Peach Jam Championship. In September 2015, Duval transferred to Advanced Preparatory International in [[Dallas, Texas]] for his junior season.{{Cite news|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2015/top-point-guard-trevon-duval-will-transfer-to-advanced-prep-international-trevon-duval-st-benedicts-trevon-duval|title=Trevon Duval transfers to Advanced Prep International|last=Jordan|first=Jason|date=Sep 7, 2015|work=usatodayhss.com|access-date=May 15, 2017}} As a junior in 2015–16, Duval averaged 16.8 [[points per game]] and 7.0 assists per game. In the spring and summer of 2016, Duval competed in the [[Under Armour]] Association circuit for the AAU team, WE-R1. He led WE-R1 to an Under Armour Association Championship, becoming the first player to win both under armour and Nike peach jam championships. Duval averaged 16.3 points per game and 3.8 assists per game in the 2016 Under Armour Association circuit.{{Cite news|url=https://www.sny.tv/college-recruiting/news/trevon-duval-wows-coaches-at-under-armour-event/172685808|title=Trevon Duval wows coaches at Under Armour Association|last=Chambers|first=Dennis|date=April 16, 2017|work=snytv.com|access-date=May 15, 2017|archive-date=August 24, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220824133513/https://www.sny.tv/college-recruiting/news/trevon-duval-wows-coaches-at-under-armour-event/172685808|url-status=dead}} Duval was then invited to the Under Armour Elite 24 in [[Brooklyn, New York]], where Duval finished the game with 25 points and 7 assists leading team drive to 140–136 victory in overtime.{{Cite news|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2016/trevon-duval-and-isaiah-washington-duel-in-first-elite-24-to-go-to-ot|title=Trevon Duval and Isaiah Washington duel in first Elite 24 to go to OT|work=usatodayhss.com|access-date=August 20, 2016}} In late 2016, Duval transferred to [[IMG Academy]] in [[Bradenton, Florida]].{{Cite news|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2016/trevon-duval-nations-no-1-point-guard-to-play-at-img-academy-fla|title=No. 1 point guard in 2017 Trevon Duval to play at IMG Academy|date=Sep 11, 2016|work=usatodayhss.com|access-date=May 15, 2017}} As a senior, Duval averaged 16.1 points per game and 7.5 assists per game leading IMG to a 26–2 record. A consensus five-star recruit, he was selected to play in the [[McDonald's All-American Game]] and [[Jordan Brand Classic]].{{Cite news|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/top-point-guard-trevon-duval-is-thankful-for-the-honor-to-play-in-the-jordan-brand-classic|title=Top point guard Trevon Duval is thankful for the honor to play in the Jordan Brand Classic|work=usatodayhss.com|access-date=March 3, 2017}} ===Recruiting=== Duval was considered one of the best players in the 2017 recruiting class and was ranked as the No.6 recruit
